title.narrative: Röster för Fred- Regional sudanesisk dialog
Voices for Peace- Regional Sudanese Dialogue

description.narrative:
Kvinnor och ungdomar utgör den demografiska majoriten av den sudanesiska befolkningen och har spelat en betydelsefull roll in de politiska demonstrationerna for fredlig och demokratisk förändring. Dessa grupper är också de mest utsatta och utgör dessutom majoriteten av befolkningen som flytt Sudan.
Fredsskapande i Sudan har ett arv av elitistism som inte lyckats förankra en fredlig eller demokratisk utveckling. Behovet av att vända sig till bredare grupper i samhället i fredsarbetet framstår som en nödvändig åtgärd.
Denna insats har sin utgångspunkt i att fred inte kan tvingas fram eller vinnas på slagfältet. Det fredsfrämjande arbetet behöver vila på ett bredare deltagande än hitills och en politisk konsensus som tar i hänsyn ett bredare folkligt perspektiv.
Denna insats tar riktning på kvinnors och ungdomars outnyttjade potential att konstruktivt bidra till det sudanesiska fredsarbetet och utveckla en regional dialog och etablera kontakter med AU, regionala institutioner och andra plattformar som har det formella medlingsuppdraget.

Women and young people make up the demographic majority of the Sudanese population and have played a significant role in the political demonstrations for peaceful and democratic change. These groups are also the most vulnerable and also make up the majority of the population who have fled Sudan. Peacemaking in Sudan has a legacy of elitism that has failed to anchor peaceful or democratic development. The need to reach out to broader groups in society in peace work appears to be a necessary measure. This effort is based on the fact that peace cannot be forced or won on the battlefield. Peace-promoting work needs to rest on broader participation than hitherto and a political consensus that takes into account a broader popular perspective. This effort addresses the untapped potential of women and young people to contribute constructively to Sudanese peace efforts and to develop a regional dialogue and establish contacts with the AU, regional institutions and other platforms that have the formal mediation mission.

The projects overall goal is "an inclusive, influential Sudanese civil society builds momentum around peaceful solutions to the conflict, within Sudan and regionally."
Underlying the main objective of trying to support a more inclusive and influential civil society are three outcomes:
1) Enhanced capacities and cohesion among engaged civil society actors, including those inside (internally) and outside Sudan (regionally), with a particular focus on women and youth.
2) Enhanced community and civil society participation in political dialogue and mediation processes at local, national, regional, and international levels, with emphasis on the meaningful engagement of women and youth.
3) An increasingly strong digital constituency for peace.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

title.narrative: Decision on Contribution RÖSTER FÖR FRED­ REGIONAL SUDANESISK DIALOG 16973

description.narrative:
Since the agreement was signed in July 2024, LPI has taken steps towards setting up the program structure.
This involves: - Selection of two Sudanese partner organisations, Wa3y and Samedia Center. - Two day virtual workshop to assess the organisational development support. - Recruitment of three Sudanese psychologists to assist in the dialogues. - Development of a training course and training the two partner organisations. - Developing methodology to healing dialogue approaches. - Launch and establishment of Sudanese civil society platforms.
The healing approach is important because many representatives of the Sudanese civil society have been exposed to deep rooted conflicts and violence which have in some cases caused post traumatic stress syndroms. In order to deal with the politics, the participants needs to be able to handle these syndroms. The program is in an early phase. Comparing the workplan for July December 2024, the most important elements seem to have been achieved. The structure, methodologies and partners are coming in place in order for the program to be implemented.
However, the actual launch of the dialogues have not taken place as anticipated. Sida assesses that this will not effect the overall implementation. In general, Sida assesses that the project is on track. The reasons for this are: LPI has laid the organisational foundation for the project and established relationships and started processes. LPI has laid the structures for a new MEL Community of Practice that support cross-organisational learning. This is important given the considerable challenges in the context. LPI demonstrate a realistic and transparent view of the challenges and has made plans and preparations to deal with these challenges. For example, it has planned to have three partner organisations, but found out late in the vetting process that one organisation took a political stance and hence would not be perceived as neutral. LPI therefore took the decision not to partner with this organisation.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
